newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: Caymans' monetary authority open for business.
newsitem.headline: Caymans' monetary authority open for business.

text.p: The newly-established Cayman Islands Monetary Authority that will oversea Cayman's lucrative offshore finance and insurance industries officially opened its doors for business Tuesday.
The authority, established as a separate entity from government, will have a supervisory and regulatory role over the banking and insurance sectors of this offshore finnacial centre and tax haven.

Speaking at an opening ceremony last Thursday before a long weekend holiday, Cayman Islands governor John Owen said the establishment of a non-governmental authority to oversee the financial industry was a logical progression in the growth of Cayman's financial industry.
It also demonstrated to the financial world that Cayman "takes its responsibilities seriously and is sending the right message to the international financial community".
Owen said Cayman was the first British territory to pass the Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty (MLAT) with U.S. regulators and also the first territory to adopt the Proceeds of Criminal Conduct Law.
That recently enacted legislation makes all money laundering a crime, not just when proceeds from drugs are involved.
"The establishment of the monetary authority sends a powerful signal that Cayman is committed to a strong regulatory regime and to the international financial community, " Owen said.
The Monetary Authority takes over a number of government functions and will operate very similar to a central bank, a government press release said.
The head of the authority is Neville Grant. It will not have jurisdiction over the recently opened Cayman Islands Stock Exchange, which operates under its own authority board.
The Caymans has 560 registered banks and financial institutions which have assets in excess of US$460 billion, according to 1996 government figures.
